title: Add phase-aware replica synchronizer and regression fanout guard
author: Marta Liu
description: Context: we observed short-lived latency regressions during staggered canary rollouts that correlate with replica warm-up timing and sporadic KV-cache invalidation. Motivation: current canary detectors can be sensitive to transient phase shifts when a subset of replicas are in different readiness phases, which generates false positives or noisy alerts and can trigger unnecessary rollbacks. This PR introduces two pieces: (1) a phase-aware replica synchronizer that annotates probe traffic with replica phase metadata and enforces a short coordination window to align probe sampling across replicas, and (2) a regression fanout guard that aggregates per-replica canary signals with tunable quorum and temporal smoothing to suppress spurious rollbacks while preserving sensitivity to sustained regressions. Design summary: the synchronizer runs as a lightweight sidecar in the probe runner and tracks replica lifecycle hooks (initialization, warm-up, steady) emitted by the serving runtime; probes in the warm-up phase are tagged and routed into a weighted sampling bucket rather than being directly included in canary statistics. The fanout guard consumes per-replica metric streams and applies a three-stage filter: per-replica anomaly detector (quantile shift with bootstrapped confidence), cross-replica consensus (weighted quorum with phase weights), and temporal dampening (exponential smoothing with configurable half-life). Config knobs: early_quorum_threshold, phase_weight_map, smoothing_half_life_seconds, max-coordinated-delay. Operational impacts: default settings are conservative to avoid masking real regressions; deployment flips are gated by Linear ENG-21345 and require a canary rollout with the sentinel probe enabled. Backwards compatibility: if the sidecar is absent, the synchronizer falls back to legacy behavior (no annotation); the fanout guard has a passthrough mode. Testing & validation: unit tests for phase transitions and weighted quorum logic included; end-to-end perf harness runs show 48% reduction in false-positive rollback triggers during synthetic staggered-rollout scenarios and a <3% increase in probe latency. Rollout plan: enable in opt-in canaries for 2 weeks, monitor false-positive rate and SLO breach delta, then flip global default with a 24-hour canary ramp. Related: builds on prior work in ENG-19702 (canary aggregation) and complements the traffic-shape-aware detector in PRs around staggered rollouts.

review_comments: Arjun Patel: Nice approach to reduce noise from warm-up replicas. Two requests: 1) add an opt-out flag at runtime in case we need to disable across a region quickly, and 2) add a short doc about how this changes the interpretation of per-replica metrics.
Marta Liu (reply): Added runtime opt-out via --synchronizer-enabled boolean and documented impact in docs/phase_synchronizer.md; left default on for opt-in canaries only.
Diego Ramirez: Fanout quorum looks good. Can you justify the default phase weights (steady=1.0, warm-up=0.2, init=0.0)? Might want to make them relative to observed latency variance.
Marta Liu (reply): Default weights chosen from A/B grid over historical rollouts; added adjustable phase_weight_map and a note in the schema for teams to tune based on measured variance.
ci_checks: perf-regression-check: pass (48% reduction in false positives on synthetic harness)
release_notes: Add phase-aware replica synchronizer and regression fanout guard to reduce spurious canary rollbacks during staggered rollouts. Default opt-in for canaries; tunable quorum and smoothing parameters. See perf-canary/docs/phase_synchronizer.md.
notes_for_ops: When enabling globally, monitor 'canary.false_positive_rate' and 'canary.quorum_disagreements' dashboards for first 72 hours. If you see sustained suppression of genuine regressions, decrease smoothing_half_life_seconds or lower early_quorum_threshold.
manual_steps: Enable feature via canary policy: 'phase_synchronizer: enabled: true' on target canary
Run a staggered-rollout synthetic job (harness/staggered_rollout_test.py) against the canary to validate behavior
